question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Back against the wall

options.text: Be in an easy situation from where escape is difficult
Be in a difficult situation from where escape is difficult
Be in a relationship which one wants to escape
Be in a difficult situation from where escape is easy

solution:
The correct answer is: **Be in a difficult situation from where escape is difficult**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom '**back against the wall**' means being in a difficult or hopeless situation. (किसी कठिन या निराशाजनक स्थिति में होना)

 
 
• **For example**: *With his back against the wall, he had no choice but to come up with a creative solution to the challenging problem.*
 
 
 
• It implies that there are no options left to escape or find a way out.
 
• The phrase is often used in situations where one is facing a challenge or an obstacle that seems insurmountable.
 
• The origin of the idiom is unclear, but it may have come from the idea of being trapped in a corner with no way out.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: It is the opposite of the correct meaning of the idiom.
 
• **Option 3**: It is not related to the idiom and is a misinterpretation.
 
• **Option 4**: It is the opposite of the correct meaning of the idiom.
